preamble: Before nasal consonants /æ/ is nasalized by coarticulation, and in several English varieties the nasalized allophone is raised into the close-mid front region, giving a raised nasal vowel of the [ẽ] ~ [ẽə] type. In Australian English (Sydney, Northern Queensland) nasalized /æ/ in words like ban overlaps /e/ in quality and stays distinct mainly by length; in the North American 'nasal system' /æ/ is raised and diphthongized to [ɛə] ~ [eə] before /m/ and /n/ (man, camp) while staying low elsewhere. The change is allophonic and limited to English varieties.

examples.note: In the nasal system (southern Midwest, northern New Jersey, Florida, parts of Canada, eastern New England), /æ/ is raised and diphthongized most strongly before /m/ and /n/; the raised vowel is also nasalized by the following nasal, while 'mat' and 'cap' keep low [æ].
Among young Sydney women an allophonic split has nasalized /æ/ raised to the /e/ area while oral /æ/ is low; the ban–Ben contrast is kept by length.
In Northern Queensland pre-nasal /e/ and /æ/ are fully neutralized in F1/F2, with /æ/ only longer.
